summary.headline: Carraro India Q2 FY27 revenue rose 19% YoY to INR6,965 million, but EBITDA margin fell to 9.2% on steel, casting and energy cost pressure.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 19% YoY and 28% QoQ to INR6,965 million, with domestic revenue up 33% and export revenue down 4% YoY. EBITDA rose 10% YoY to INR652 million, but margin slipped to 9.2% from 10%, with gross margin at 23.3% versus 26.4%. Management attributed the squeeze to lagged steel and casting indexation (3 to 6 months) and unindexed energy, freight and supplier labour costs, which are being recovered through separate customer negotiations. Management reaffirmed 10-15% revenue growth for FY27 and a double-digit EBITDA margin outcome, while pointing to H2 margin improvement as recoveries come through.

financial_highlights.change: +8% YoY; margin vs 10.4% in H1 FY26
vs about 27.5% in H1 FY26, roughly 200 bps lower

segments.name: Agricultural (Q2)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3,300 million, up 29% YoY. H1 agri revenue INR5,859 million, up 23%; H1 domestic agri about INR4,800 million (+34%) and export agri about INR105 million (-12%).

segments.name: Construction Equipment (Q2)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2,979 million, up 12% YoY. H1 construction equipment INR5,243 million, up 8%; H1 export construction about INR198 crore (INR1,980 million) vs INR228 crore last year, domestic construction about INR327 crore vs INR256 crore.

segments.name: Others (gears, spare parts, engineering services) (Q2)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR686 million, up 9% YoY. H1 Others INR1,309 million, up 13%. Engineering services revenue is being de-emphasised as a standalone stream.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Q2 domestic revenue INR4,859 million (+33% YoY), about 70% of H1 revenue. Q2 export INR2,106 million (-4% YoY, +27% QoQ). H1 domestic INR8,654 million (+30%); H1 export INR3,758 million vs INR4,113 million.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth expected within the 10-15% target range; H1 growth of 15% sits at the top of that range.
Management guides for FY27 revenue of close to INR2,500 crore, and at least 10% revenue growth in FY28 (a feeler from customers, described as early).
EBITDA: management's realistic guidance is double-digit margin for FY27 (10% or above), versus the earlier 11-11.3% guidance, contingent on the West Asia conflict easing.
Commitment to continued growth in absolute EBITDA in FY27; margins expected to improve progressively as price recoveries and localization catch up.
Export outlook: Q3 and Q4 expected to replicate Q2 levels; FY27 exports flat to minor growth. Management expects H2 export YoY to be flattish to slightly up.
Long-term aspiration of EUR350-400 million (about INR3,500 crore) turnover by 2030 is maintained.
Capex: H2 FY27 to be more capital intensive; FY27 capex about INR100 crore-plus, with 70-80% likely to be spent and similar amount in FY28 (FY28 budget not yet approved).
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex INR204 million (about INR20 crore), below budget; H2 expected to be more capital intensive.
Paint shop building construction commenced; side-drive sub-assembly line and backlash machine commissioned to add portal axle and 4-wheel drive differential capacity.
Raw material localisation recovered to about 80% in Q2 FY27 from 74% in Q1; target 86-88%.
Third authorised service centre agreement signed for aftermarket reach.
Tele-boom handler: two programmes in series production; 4-5 more at prototype or field validation; capacity constraints noted for supplying the global OEM's demand.
demand_pricing: Domestic 4-wheel drive (4WD) adoption is rising; industry 4WD penetration estimated at about 23-25% (unofficial), with management expecting 27-28% in coming months and a long-run target of 35-40%. Carraro's non-captive 4WD market share is cited at 55-59%.
About 2% of H1 domestic growth came from price increases; clean domestic volume growth estimated at 12-13% YoY.
Pass-through negotiations on energy, freight and supplier labour: 30-40% of customer negotiations still open; management expects initial benefits from Q3 FY27.
Export softness: logistics not yet normalised; Turkey slowed in Q2, Europe agriculture weak, Latin America agri down; Africa/Algeria showed some traction.
Tele-boom handler export: management expects about INR180 crore in FY27 (55-60% of a 3-3.5 year INR300 crore target), and about INR300 crore in FY28-29 from the global OEM.
Indian tele-boom handler market about 800 machines in H1 FY27 vs 300-400 earlier per half-year, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How much of H1 domestic 30% growth is price versus volume, and how are the remaining cost pass-through negotiations going?
qa_highlights.answer: About 2% of growth is price, leaving clean growth of 12-13%. Management says customers agree in principle to pass-through, 30-40% of negotiations remain open, and initial benefits should show from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will export revenue be flat YoY in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a flattish to slightly up H2 export trend, citing logistics and uneven regional demand; Davide said Q2 run-rate could repeat in Q3 and Q4, implying a minor or flat full year.

qa_highlights.question: Are there sizing or status updates on the tele-boom handler programmes and their FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the global OEM programme is on track, with about INR180 crore expected in FY27 and about INR300 crore in FY28-29; new domestic programmes will ramp from FY28 mid-year onward.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company expect double-digit growth and margin guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FY27 revenue near INR2,500 crore and at least 10% growth next year. EBITDA margin guided to 10% or above for FY27, down from the earlier 11-11.3% range, given the unresolved conflict.

qa_highlights.question: What are the corporate services and legal/professional fee items in other expenses?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate services are central group IT and shared-function allocations. Professional fees include R&D spend, which rose after the company bought the IP from headquarters and replaced royalties; management says this cost has reached a natural level.

qa_highlights.question: Is the captive threat to 4WD business real, and can customers use 4WD axles on 2WD tractors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 4WD axles cannot be used on 2WD tractors. Captive risk is limited because co-designing, time to market and technology partnership keep OEMs with Carraro; there have been no revenue drops from any customer in 30 years.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on pass-through negotiations; 30-40% of customer talks are still open and the timing is uncertain.
Input costs (steel, castings, energy, freight) were still rising into Q3 per management, with recoveries lagging by 3-6 months.
Export recovery is uneven: Turkey, Europe, and Latin America weakened in Q2 and logistics remain unresolved.
Engineering services revenue has been scaled back; management is shifting to co-design rather than standalone revenue.
Localisation (80%) is below the 86-88% target, and imports by air freight were needed in Q1.
FY28 capex plan is not yet approved and FY27 capex may slip by 20-30% into FY28.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic on revenue and domestic 4WD demand, but explicitly measured and less specific on profitability. Management has lowered its margin expectation to double-digit and attributes the shortfall to the West Asia conflict, while saying recoveries are constructive but still incomplete.
key_quotes: Our commitment for FY27 is continued growth in absolute EBITDA.
We are confident that we should achieve a double digit at least for this year closure.
But 4-wheel drive adoption is structural rather than cyclical.

adds.what: Side-drive sub-assembly line and backlash machine commissioned (portal axle and 4WD differential capacity)

growth.why: Management reaffirmed FY27 revenue of close to INR2,500 crore (10-15% growth, H1 at +15%) and at least 10% growth in FY28, backed by 4WD share gains, tele-boom handler orders (about INR180 crore FY27 export expected) and a commissioned side-drive line, but export growth is flat and the 30-40% of open price pass-through negotiations are unresolved; EBITDA margin guide was cut to 10%+ from 11-11.3%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 9.2% in Q2 (H1 9.7% vs 10.4%) with gross margin 23.3% vs 26.4%, but management expects progressive improvement as pass-through recoveries start from Q3 FY27 with 30-40% of negotiations still open; FY27 guide is 10%+ versus earlier 11-11.3%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Side-drive sub-assembly line and backlash machine already commissioned and paint shop under construction, but no major new plant is guided and H2 capex is only ramping from about INR20 crore in H1 against a INR100-plus crore FY27 plan.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Clean domestic volume growth of 12-13% YoY (about 2% of H1 domestic growth was price), 4WD penetration rising to 27-28% from 23-25%, and tele-boom handler export expected at about INR180 crore in FY27; exports flat in H2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex of INR100-plus crore with 70-80% likely to be spent and an FY28 budget of similar size not yet approved; utilisation was not quantified, so a new capex announcement is conditional on the FY28 budget.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management cut the FY27 EBITDA margin guide to 10%+ from 11-11.3% and says it is contingent on West Asia easing; revenue guide of about INR2,500 crore is only held, not raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Input costs (steel, castings, energy, freight) were still rising into Q3 with 3-6 month indexation lag, 30-40% of pass-through talks open, and the margin guide already cut once.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Tele-boom handler export programme of about INR300 crore expected in FY28-29 from the global OEM, with two programmes in series production and 4-5 at prototype; new domestic programmes ramp from FY28 mid-year.

rows.label: Cost pass-through recoveries from Q3 FY27
rows.why: Customers agree in principle to pass through energy, freight and labour costs, with 30-40% of negotiations still open and initial benefits expected from Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Tele-boom handler global OEM orders
rows.why: About INR180 crore expected in FY27 and about INR300 crore in FY28-29 from the global OEM, on track per management, though capacity constraints are noted.

rows.label: Export recovery
rows.why: Export revenue fell 4% YoY in Q2 (H1 INR3,758 million vs INR4,113 million), management expects H2 exports flattish to slightly up, with Turkey, Europe and Latin America weak.

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic 4WD demand, tele-boom orders and FY27 revenue near INR2,500 crore, but cautious on profitability, cutting the margin guide to 10%+ and tying it to West Asia easing. Analysts pressed on price versus volume, pass-through progress and the export outlook.

oneOffs.what: No one-off item quantified; brief shows no excluded or exceptional item in Q2 FY27 growth

quality.why: Q2 revenue grew 19% YoY, with roughly 12-13% clean domestic volume growth in H1 and only about 2% from price, so growth is driven by volume (mainly 4WD axles in agri, plus construction equipment) rather than one-offs, though export fell 4% YoY and the 12-13% volume figure is an H1 estimate.
